mn3:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn3:1.3: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn3:2.1: ‘Bhikkhus, be my heirs in Dhamma, not my heirs in material things.
mn3:2.2: Out of pity for you I have thought:
mn3:2.3: “How shall my disciples be my heirs in Dhamma, not my heirs in material things?”
mn3:2.4: If you are my heirs in material things, not my heirs in Dhamma, it will be a reproach to you:
mn3:2.5: “The Master’s disciples live as his heirs in material things, not as his heirs in Dhamma”,
mn3:2.6: and it will be a reproach to me that
mn3:2.7: “The Master’s disciples live as his heirs in material things, not as his heirs in Dhamma”.
mn3:2.8: If you are my heirs in Dhamma, not my heirs in material things, it will be no reproach to you that
mn3:2.9: “The Master’s disciples live as his heirs in Dhamma, not as his heirs in material things”,
mn3:2.10: and it will be no reproach to me that
mn3:2.11: “The Master’s disciples live as his heirs in Dhamma, not as his heirs in material things”.
mn3:2.12: Therefore, bhikkhus, be my heirs in Dhamma, not my heirs in material things.
mn3:2.13: Out of pity for you I have thought:
mn3:2.14: “How shall my disciples be my heirs in Dhamma, not my heirs in material things?”
mn3:3.1: Now, bhikkhus, suppose that I had eaten, refused more, had my fill, finished, had enough, had what I needed,
mn3:3.2: and some alms-food was left over to be thrown away.
mn3:3.3: Then two bhikkhus arrived hungry and weak,
mn3:3.5: “Bhikkhus, I have eaten, refused more … had what I needed,
mn3:3.6: but there is this alms-food of mine left over to be thrown away;
mn3:3.7: eat if you like; if you do not then I shall throw it now where there is no greenery or drop into water where there is no life”;
mn3:3.9: “The Blessed One has eaten, refused more … had what he needed,
mn3:3.10: but there is this alms-food of the Blessed One left over to be thrown away;
mn3:3.11: if we do not eat it the Blessed One will throw it away …
mn3:3.12: but this has been said by the Blessed One:
mn3:3.13: ‘Bhikkhus, be my heirs in Dhamma, not my heirs in material things’:
mn3:3.14: now this alms-food is one of the material things;
mn3:3.15: suppose that instead of eating this alms-food I pass the night and day hungry and weak?”
mn3:3.16: and instead of eating that alms-food he passed that night and day hungry and weak;
mn3:3.18: “The Blessed One has eaten … had what he needed,
mn3:3.19: but there is this alms-food of the Blessed One’s left over to be thrown away …
mn3:3.21: Suppose that I eat this alms-food and pass the night and day neither hungry nor weak?”
mn3:3.22: And after eating that alms-food he passed the night and day not hungry and weak.
mn3:3.23: Now although that bhikkhu by eating that alms-food passed the night and day neither hungry nor weak, yet the first bhikkhu is more to be respected and commended by me.
mn3:3.25: Because that will for long conduce to his fewness of wishes, contentment, effacement, easy support and arousal of energy.
mn3:3.26: Therefore, bhikkhus, be my heirs in Dhamma, not my heirs in material things.
mn3:3.27: Out of pity for you I have thought:
mn3:3.28: “How shall my disciples be my heirs in Dhamma, not my heirs in material things?”’
mn3:4.1: That is what the Blessed One said.
mn3:4.2: Having said that, he rose from his seat and went into his dwelling.
mn3:4.3: Soon after he had gone, the venerable Sāriputta addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn3:5.1: ‘Friends, in what way do disciples of a Master who lives secluded not train in seclusion? And in what way do disciples of a Master who lives secluded train in seclusion?’
mn3:5.2: ‘Indeed, friend, we would come from far away to learn from the venerable Sāriputta the meaning of this pronouncement.
mn3:5.3: It would be good if the meaning of this pronouncement would occur to the venerable Sāriputta;
mn3:5.4: having heard it from him, the bhikkhus will remember it.’
mn3:5.5: ‘Then, listen and heed well what I shall say.’
mn3:6.1: ‘Friends, in what way do disciples of a Master who lives secluded not train in seclusion?
mn3:6.2: Here, friends, disciples of a Master who lives secluded do not train in seclusion,
mn3:6.3: they do not abandon what the Master tells them to abandon,
mn3:6.4: they are busy and careless, forward in erring, giving up seclusion.
mn3:6.5: In this the elder bhikkhus are to be blamed for three reasons.
mn3:6.6: ‘As disciples of a Master who lives secluded they do not train in seclusion’:
mn3:6.7: they are to be blamed for this first reason.
mn3:6.8: ‘They do not abandon what the Master tells them to abandon’:
mn3:6.9: they are to be blamed for this second reason.
mn3:6.10: ‘They are busy, careless, forward in erring, giving up seclusion’:
mn3:6.11: they are to be blamed for this third reason.
mn3:6.12: The elder bhikkhus are to be blamed for these three reasons.
mn3:6.13: In this the middle bhikkhus are to be blamed for three reasons …
mn3:6.14: In this the new bhikkhus are to be blamed for three reasons.
mn3:6.15: ‘As disciples of a Master who lives secluded they do not train in seclusion’:
mn3:6.16: they are to be blamed for this first reason.
mn3:6.17: ‘They do not abandon what the Master tells them to abandon’:
mn3:6.18: they are to be blamed for this second reason.
mn3:6.19: ‘They are busy, careless, forward in erring, giving up seclusion’:
mn3:6.20: they are to be blamed for this third reason.
mn3:6.21: The new bhikkhus are to be blamed for these three reasons.
mn3:6.22: It is in this way that disciples of a Master who lives secluded do not train in seclusion.
mn3:7.1: ‘In what way do disciples of a Master who lives secluded train in seclusion?
mn3:7.2: Here, disciples of a Master who lives secluded train in seclusion;
mn3:7.3: they abandon what the Master tells them to abandon;
mn3:7.4: they are not busy and not careless, they give up erring and are forward in seclusion.
mn3:7.5: In this the elder bhikkhus are to be commended for three reasons.
mn3:7.6: ‘As disciples of a Master who lives secluded they train in seclusion’:
mn3:7.7: they are to be commended for this first reason.
mn3:7.8: ‘They abandon what the Master tells them to abandon’:
mn3:7.9: they are to be commended for this second reason.
mn3:7.10: ‘They are not busy and not careless; they give up erring and are forward in seclusion’:
mn3:7.11: they are to be commended for this third reason.
mn3:7.12: The elder bhikkhus are to be commended for these three reasons.
mn3:7.13: In this the middle bhikkhus are to be commended for three reasons …
mn3:7.14: In this the new bhikkhus are to be commended for three reasons.
mn3:7.15: ‘As disciples of a Master who lives secluded they train in seclusion’:
mn3:7.16: they are to be commended for this first reason.
mn3:7.17: ‘They abandon what the Master tells them to abandon’:
mn3:7.18: they are to be commended for this second reason.
mn3:7.19: ‘They are not busy and not careless; they give up erring and are forward in seclusion’:
mn3:7.20: they are to be commended for this third reason.
mn3:7.21: The new bhikkhus are to be commended for these three reasons.
mn3:7.22: It is in this way that the disciples of a Master who lives secluded train in seclusion.
mn3:8.1: ‘Friends, the evil herein is greed and it is hate.
mn3:8.2: There is a Middle Way for the abandoning of greed and hate, giving vision, giving knowledge, that leads to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.
mn3:8.3: And what is that Middle Way?
mn3:8.4: It is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn3:8.5: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.
mn3:8.6: This is the Middle Way giving vision, giving knowledge, that leads to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.
mn3:9-15.1: ‘Friends, the evil herein is anger and it is revenge …
mn3:9-15.2: the evil herein is contempt and it is domineering,
mn3:9-15.3: the evil herein is envy and it is avarice,
mn3:9-15.4: the evil herein is deceit and it is fraud,
mn3:9-15.5: the evil herein is obduracy and it is presumption,
mn3:9-15.6: the evil herein is conceit and it is pride (haughtiness),
mn3:9-15.7: the evil herein is vanity and it is negligence.
mn3:9-15.8: There is a Middle Way for the abandoning of vanity and negligence, giving vision, giving knowledge, that leads to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.
mn3:9-15.9: And what is that Middle Way?
mn3:9-15.10: It is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is to say,
mn3:9-15.11: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.
mn3:9-15.12: This is the Middle Way giving vision, giving knowledge, that leads to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.’”
mn3:9-15.13: That is what the venerable Sāriputta said.
mn3:9-15.14: The bhikkhus were satisfied, and they delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words.
